title: Jailer 2 Crosses Rs 500 Crore in Six Days, Fastest Tamil Film Ever
excerpt: A record Rs 42.35 crore first Monday took the Rajinikanth sequel to Rs 477.75 crore in five days, and Day 6 bookings carried it past the milestone
body:
• Jailer 2 crossed Rs 500 crore worldwide on its sixth day, becoming the fastest Tamil film ever to reach the mark, according to tracker Sacnilk.
  • Its fifth day, the first Monday, delivered a record Rs 42.35 crore net in India, taking the five-day worldwide gross to Rs 477.75 crore.
  • The Rajinikanth sequel is now the third-biggest Indian film of 2026, passing Border 2 and Hanuman Ansh, and sixth on the all-time Tamil list.
  • North America has grossed $5.2 million, including a No. 9 finish in the US weekend chart, underlining how much overseas business is driving the run.

Jailer 2 has crossed Rs 500 crore at the worldwide box office in six days, the fastest any Tamil film has reached the milestone. Tracker Sacnilk reported that the Rajinikanth sequel entered Tuesday needing only about Rs 22.25 crore more, and that Day 6 advance bookings in India alone, worth Rs 22.35 crore, pushed its combined tally past Rs 500 crore. It is only the fifth Tamil release ever to join the Rs 500 crore club, and Rajinikanth accounts for four of those five entries.

A Record Monday Set Up the Crossing

The new development is the strength of the film's first Monday. On Day 5, October 19, Jailer 2 collected Rs 42.35 crore net in India, the highest Monday collection recorded by a Tamil film, according to Sacnilk figures reported by multiple outlets. The drop from Sunday's Rs 55.85 crore was 24.2 percent, a hold helped by the festive holiday period. That took the five-day India net to Rs 242.25 crore and the India gross to Rs 283.75 crore, while overseas reached Rs 194 crore, for a five-day worldwide gross of Rs 477.75 crore. The Tamil version led Monday with Rs 31.40 crore, followed by Telugu at Rs 7.15 crore, Hindi at Rs 3.35 crore and Kannada at Rs 45 lakh. Trackers differ slightly on the five-day worldwide total: Koimoi put it at Rs 478.86 crore, about Rs 1 crore above the Sacnilk tally used by most outlets.

Where the Film Stands Now

With that Monday, Jailer 2 became the third-highest-grossing Indian film of 2026, overtaking the lifetime totals of Border 2 (Rs 464 crore) and Hanuman Ansh (Rs 439 crore), Hindustan Times reported. It now trails only Dhurandhar: The Revenge (Rs 1,852 crore) and Drishyam 3 (Rs 538 crore). On the all-time Tamil chart it sits sixth after five days, behind 2.0 (Rs 691 crore) and within reach of Ponniyin Selvan: I (Rs 488 crore) and Coolie (Rs 518 crore). Koimoi also reported that the two-film Jailer franchise has passed Rs 1,000 crore combined worldwide. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, the sequel returns Rajinikanth as retired jailer Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, the role he created in the 2023 hit Jailer, with music by Anirudh Ravichander and cameos by Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar, Hrithik Roshan and Jackie Shroff.

Overseas Business Is Carrying Half the Story

For diaspora audiences, the striking part of this update is where the money is coming from. Hindustan Times reported overseas collections of $20.5 million in five days. In North America, where Shloka Entertainments distributed the film, Jailer 2 grossed $3.2 million from Friday to Sunday to finish ninth in the US weekend chart, taking its regional total to $5.2 million, according to Rentrak estimates cited by Variety and reported by Livemint. The same estimates made it the second-biggest film worldwide over the October 16-18 weekend, with $31.2 million, behind only Street Fighter at $51.1 million.

What Comes Next

The next markers are Drishyam 3's Rs 538 crore, the original Jailer's lifetime gross of about Rs 605 crore, and a second weekend that falls after the festive period ends. Director Nelson Dilipkumar, posting on X during the opening weekend, wrote: "Theatres are going bonkers! Thalaivar magic hits different. Thank you, dear audience, for the phenomenal love and reception for #Jailer2," The Indian Express reported.
